material_systems.name: Solvent-Based MDF Edge Sealer

primer.notes: MUST be applied to MDF cut/routed edges BEFORE any latex product. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber swelling on MDF edges. Step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine §2.1 and §4.1.

material_systems.notes: Edge-only application. Step 1 of MDF two-step prime process. Wood wall MDF panels have routed profiles and cut edges at panel joints — all must be sealed before latex primer.

material_systems.name: High-Build Latex Face Primer for MDF

primer.notes: Applied to MDF face surfaces AFTER edge sealing with shellac/oil-based. Builds film, levels surface. Step 2 of two-step MDF prime.

material_systems.notes: Step 2 of MDF two-step prime. Face surfaces only — edges already sealed.

material_systems.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for FJP/Poplar

products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Oil-Based Primer
primer.notes: MANDATORY for bare FJP. Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through standard latex primers without stain-blocking. NOT optional. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine §2.2 and §4.1.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Stain-blocking is not optional for FJP wood wall panels/boards.

material_systems.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood

primer.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut, maple). Per Millwork Doctrine §4.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Required for all bare hardwood wood wall substrates.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Wood Primer for Softwood

primer.notes: Standard primer-sealer for bare softwood wall panels/boards. Seals and provides tooth for finish coat.

material_systems.notes: Substrate-driven. Reuse from SF_WINDOW_INT_NC. REUSE OVER CREATION.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel

products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
finish.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Large wood wall areas benefit from fast dry for efficient multi-coat workflow. Same system as trim, window, riser, and wainscot specs.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate (FFD §4.1). Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel

products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
finish.notes: Superior flow and leveling — critical for large flat wood wall panels where brush marks are highly visible. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). On tall walls, manage open time carefully — large contiguous surfaces amplify temperature sensitivity. Same system as trim, window, riser, and wainscot specs.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel

finish.coat_notes: QT5 brush/roll typically requires 3+ coats per FFD §15.10.3.
finish.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Same system as trim, window, riser, and wainscot specs.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion (RC-005).

coverage_profiles.notes: Wood wall panel/board primer coverage. SF measured directly from PaintScope input — no conversion needed. MDF edges may absorb more sealer. Library panel 3D profiles add ~10% surface area over measured wall SF. Shiplap/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% effective surface area.
assumptions: Single coat primer system (except MDF two-step: edge seal + face prime)
Wood wall SF from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WOOD_WALL

coverage_profiles.notes: Wood wall panel/board finish coat coverage on primed smooth surface. Two-coat standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage. Library panel may consume ~10% more material due to increased surface area from 3D profile with rails and stiles. Shiplap/T&G groove detail also increases material consumption ~5-10% due to paint in grooves. Spray method: add 20-30% waste for overspray on board/panel work.
assumptions: Wood wall SF from PaintScope input
Library panel 3D profile adds ~10% to effective surface area
Shiplap/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% to effective surface area

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.usage: Floor protection runners at base of wood wall work area
consumables.notes: Runner-style for wood wall base perimeter. Full-height wall increases drip risk from brush/spray and sanding dust — especially on tall walls where gravity causes paint to run. Always required regardless of application method.

consumables.name: Masking tape (1.5" blue painter's tape)
consumables.usage: Ceiling masking at ceiling-wall junction (spray only), general edge masking
consumables.notes: 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. Ceiling masking required only for spray application method. Tape line at ceiling-wall junction — paper hangs down from tape edge.

consumables.name: Masking paper (12-inch)
consumables.usage: Ceiling surface masking at ceiling-wall junction (spray only)
consumables.notes: Paper + tape system for ceiling protection at ceiling-wall junction during spray application. 12-inch width adequate for overspray drift from wall-height spray work. Unlike wainscot (wall_adjacent zone above cap rail), wood wall uses ceiling_line zone — paper masks ceiling surface rather than wall above.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer sanding for bare substrates, factory primer scuff
consumables.notes: 150 grit for initial bare wood sanding and factory primer scuff. Hand sanding or pad sanding. On tall walls (H2+), pole sander may be used for field work above reach height.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.usage: Pre-primer final sand, between-coat sanding (QT3 spot, QT4 full)
consumables.notes: 220 grit for final prep sand and between-coat sanding. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge acceptable for shiplap/T&G grooves and library panel profiles.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.notes: 220-320 grit range at QT5. Uniform scratch pattern required. Flexible sanding sponge for groove/profile detail work.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.usage: Rigid block for between-coat sanding. Mandatory per FFD §15.4.1.
consumables.notes: One block per crew, reusable. Rigid block critical for flat panel and board surfaces to avoid creating waves. Large flat wood wall areas particularly benefit from rigid block leveling of brush marks.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5")
consumables.usage: Primary brush for wood wall panel faces, frame detail (library panel), and cutting-in
consumables.notes: 2-2.5 inch for flat panel faces, board faces, and library panel frame detail. One per painter per material change.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411
consumables.usage: Fine atomization for wood wall panel/board spray finish
consumables.notes: Tight fan pattern for wood wall work. Broad sweep passes for flat panel and board styles (shiplap, T&G); fine detail for library panel frame profiles. On tall walls, maintain consistent distance from top to bottom to avoid drip accumulation.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.usage: Remove sanding dust before each coat application
consumables.notes: One tack cloth covers ~30 SF of wood wall surface. Use before every coat. Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) generate more sanding dust from groove detail.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.usage: Board/panel joints and perimeter junctions (wall-to-ceiling, wall-to-floor)
consumables.notes: Joint types vary by wall_style: (1) Board styles (shiplap, T&G) — board-to-board joints (high density, ~1.5 LF joints per SF for 6-inch boards). Shiplap V-grooves may be left uncaulked by design to preserve board definition. (2) Panel styles (flat_panel, library_panel) — panel-to-frame joints (horizontal and vertical internal joints). (3) ALL styles — perimeter caulk at wall-to-ceiling junction and wall-to-floor junction. Flexible caulk accommodates seasonal wood movement — critical for board-style walls.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackle compound
consumables.usage: Fill fastener holes on wood wall panels/boards
consumables.notes: ELEVATED CONSUMPTION on board-style walls (shiplap, T&G). Each board is face-nailed at every stud — high fastener hole density. NC fastener fill uses overfill-sand-flush method with HIGH waste factor per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine. Panel styles (flat_panel, library_panel) have fewer visible fasteners — internal framing is typically hidden. Yield estimate of 80 SF/QT is average across all wall styles; board styles may consume 50% more.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.usage: Fill deeper defects, damaged board/panel edges, and knot holes on wood wall surfaces
consumables.notes: Lightweight or auto-body type depending on defect depth. Supplement to spackle for deeper fills. One quart per ~100 SF of wood wall assembly.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners at base of wood wall work area
floor_perimeter.condition: ALWAYS — wood wall is floor-to-ceiling, drip and dust protection mandatory. Full-height walls increase drip risk from gravity especially on tall walls (H2+).

ceiling_line.description: Paper masking at ceiling-wall junction to protect finished ceiling from overspray

required_inputs.purpose: Floor protection area at wood wall work zone
Ceiling masking LF at ceiling-wall junction (spray only)
Height classification for modifier selection — wood wall height varies by room

compatibility_rules.description: All finish systems are compatible with all primer systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer and finish are independent selections. All combinations valid.

compatibility_rules.description: SS_PRIMED_FACTORY compatible with all finish systems
compatibility_rules.notes: Scuff sand factory primer for adhesion. No additional primer needed.

compatibility_rules.description: MDF two-step prime: shellac edge seal MUST precede latex face prime
compatibility_rules.notes: SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC on edges first, then SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX on faces. Never reverse. Water-based products on raw MDF edges cause irreversible fiber swelling.

risk_notes.topic: MDF fiber swelling on routed edges
risk_notes.risk: Irreversible fiber swelling if water-based product contacts raw MDF cut/routed edges — wood wall MDF panels have routed profiles at panel-to-frame joints
risk_notes.mitigation: Always seal MDF edges with shellac/oil-based sealer (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC) before any latex product. MDF wood wall panels may have extensive routed profiles depending on wall_style.

risk_notes.risk: Resin and green mineral streaks bleed through non-stain-blocking primer on bare FJP
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK. Stain-blocking is MANDATORY for bare FJP wood wall panels/boards.

risk_notes.risk: Tannin bleed re-emerges through multiple finish coats on bare hardwood
risk_notes.mitigation: Use SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK. Required for all bare hardwood wood wall substrates.

risk_notes.risk: Excessive paint buildup in shiplap V-grooves or T&G joints, losing board definition and groove profile
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats on board-style walls. Spray preferred — atomized application minimizes groove fill. If brushing, use brush sized to groove width. Avoid over-application. Multiple thin coats better than one heavy coat.

risk_notes.topic: Brush marks on large flat panel/board areas
risk_notes.risk: Visible brush marks on large flat surfaces from overworking waterborne product — amplified on wood walls due to large contiguous area
risk_notes.mitigation: Waterborne philosophy (FFD §15.3.1): Apply, tip once, walk away. Roll and Tip on flat panels (FFD §15.6). Sand out marks between coats with rigid block (FFD §15.4.1). Large wood wall areas amplify this risk — work in manageable sections.

risk_notes.topic: Library panel detail holidays at frame-to-panel transitions
risk_notes.risk: Incomplete coverage in library panel recessed profiles at panel-to-frame transitions
risk_notes.mitigation: Spray technique: field panels first, then HVLP for frame detail. Brush: work panel-to-frame sequence. Check all recessed profiles for holidays during interstage inspection.

risk_notes.topic: Height-related drip accumulation on tall walls
risk_notes.risk: Gravity causes paint to run and accumulate on lower portions of tall (12+ ft) walls during spray or heavy brush application. Unlike wainscot (always H1, 32-42 inches), wood walls span floor to ceiling with variable height.
risk_notes.mitigation: Apply thinner coats on tall walls. For spray: maintain consistent distance and speed from top to bottom. For brush: watch for runs collecting on lower boards/panels — back-check lower sections while upper sections are still wet. At H2+ heights, plan top-down application with attention to lower-section drip check.

risk_notes.topic: Board joint caulk failure from wood movement
risk_notes.risk: Seasonal expansion/contraction of wood wall boards causes caulk cracking at board-to-board joints. Shiplap boards move more than T&G due to less constraint at joints.
risk_notes.mitigation: Use quality paintable acrylic latex caulk with flexibility. Apply after primer cure when possible. Proper joint width. Shiplap V-groove joints may be left uncaulked by design to accommodate movement and preserve board-line aesthetic.

material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are substrate-driven with 5 distinct paths (MDF edge seal, MDF face prime, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood standard). (2) Finish systems are QT-driven (SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, SYS_FF_PREMIUM). Any primer can pair with any finish. Identical architecture to SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC.
material_notes.mdf_two_step_note: MDF requires two-step prime: edge seal with shellac/oil-based (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC), then face prime with latex (SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX). Order is mandatory. Wood wall MDF panels have routed profiles at panel joints — edge area varies by wall_style.
material_notes.coverage_note: Wood wall SF directly from PaintScope input PS_SURFACE_SF.WOOD_WALL — no conversion needed. Library panel adds ~10% effective surface area over measured wall SF due to 3D profile. Shiplap/T&G groove detail adds ~5-10% effective surface area.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel (RC-006).
material_notes.caulk_joint_types: Joint types vary by wall_style: (1) Board styles (shiplap, T&G) — board-to-board joints at high density; shiplap V-grooves may be uncaulked by design. (2) Panel styles (flat_panel, library_panel) — panel-to-frame joints (horizontal and vertical internal). (3) ALL styles — perimeter caulk at wall-to-ceiling and wall-to-floor junctions.
material_notes.elevated_spackle_note: Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) have high fastener density — each board is face-nailed at every stud. Spackle consumption for fastener filling will be significantly higher than panel-style walls (flat_panel, library_panel) where internal framing is typically hidden. NC fastener fill uses overfill-sand-flush method with HIGH waste factor per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine.
material_notes.height_note: Unlike SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC (always H1, 32-42 inches), wood wall height varies by room. Height modifier applied by estimation engine via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND per room. Tall walls amplify drip risk, temperature sensitivity for open time management, and spray technique requirements.
material_notes.ceiling_line_vs_wall_adjacent: Key distinction from SF_WAINSCOT_PANEL_NC: wainscot uses wall_adjacent zone (masking wall above cap rail) with PS_PROTECT_LF.WALL_ADJACENT. Wood wall uses ceiling_line zone (masking ceiling at wall-ceiling junction) with PS_PROTECT_LF.CEILING_LINE. No cap rail intermediary.

assumptions.value: 350-450 SF/gal for finish coat on primed smooth surface
assumptions.source: Manufacturer PDS data, aligned with trim/window/riser/wainscot spec coverage

assumptions.value: ~10% more material consumption for library panel due to 3D profile with rails and stiles
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical panel profile depth — same rationale as raised_panel in wainscot
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides library panel surface area multiplier. 10% is conservative estimate for standard profile depths.

assumptions.value: ~5-10% more material consumption for shiplap/T&G due to paint in groove detail
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on groove dimensions and board width
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides board groove material multiplier. 5-10% is conservative for standard V-groove and T&G profiles.

assumptions.value: Board-to-board joint density ~1.5 LF joints per SF for 6-inch boards; panel-to-frame density lower and similar to wainscot
assumptions.source: Research estimate based on typical board dimensions and stud spacing
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines board joint density for wood wall styles. Caulk consumption estimated per wall SF with wall_style as the density driver.

assumptions.value: Board-style walls (shiplap, T&G) may consume 50% more spackle than panel-style walls due to fastener density
assumptions.source: Research estimate RF-014 based on fastener count per board at 16 in OC stud spacing
assumptions.note: No doctrine provides wall-style-specific spackle consumption rates. 50% increase is conservative for high-density fastener fill on board-style walls.
